# Acme — Staff PM

## Standard
- Partner ecosystem / platform PM experience, stated plainly
- Cross-functional team leadership at 5+ people
- Quantified revenue or efficiency impact
- 2-page target
- check_materials.py clean
- language checker clean

## Coverage
| requirement | status | evidence | decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| partner ecosystem experience | have | Fernbridge Data partner API work | answered |
| cross-functional leadership | have | led 6 engineers, 2 designers | answered |
| enterprise billing platform experience | shown-but-unnamed | Cascade Systems billing platform bullet exists but doesn't use the word "billing" in the Summary | answered |

## Selection
| # | role | bullet | in/out | source | words | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fernbridge Data | Took the partner API from an internal afterthought to 40% of new-logo revenue in 18 months | in | base | 17 | strongest match to the JD's ecosystem ask |
| 2 | Fernbridge Data | Instrumented the partner funnel and shipped only what the data showed partners were blocked on | in | base | 16 | shows the same data-first approach the JD's culture section describes |
| 3 | Fernbridge Data | Led a cross-functional team of 6 engineers and 2 designers on the ecosystem roadmap | in | base | 14 | answers the leadership requirement directly |
| 4 | Cascade Systems | Owned the core billing platform used by 400+ enterprise customers | out | base | 11 | weakest fit for this JD; page budget cut here first |
| 5 | Cascade Systems | Cut onboarding time from 6 weeks to 9 days by redesigning the setup flow | out | base | 13 | second-weakest fit; earlier role, less ecosystem-relevant |
Dear Acme Hiring Team,

I lead platform roadmaps for B2B SaaS products where the ecosystem, not any single feature, is the moat, which is the bet your Staff PM posting is making. Over the last five years I have watched the same pattern play out at two different companies: the product that wins is the one whose partners can build on it without waiting for a roadmap slot, and the team that gets there first is the team that treats the partner surface as its own product from day one.

At Fernbridge Data I took our partner API from an internal afterthought to 40% of new-logo revenue in 18 months. The turn came from instrumenting the partner funnel before writing a line of new API surface, so every build decision traced back to where partners were actually stuck, not where we assumed they were stuck. That same discipline carried into the billing platform work earlier in my career at Cascade Systems, where a redesigned onboarding flow cut time-to-value from six weeks to nine days for over 400 enterprise customers.

Your posting describes the same inflection point Acme is at with its own ecosystem: real usage, an unclear next layer, and a decision about whether the partner experience gets a dedicated roadmap or stays a side project. I would bring the same approach: instrument first, then build only what the data says partners are blocked on, and keep the roadmap honest about the tradeoff between platform depth and shipping speed.

I would welcome the chance to talk about where Acme's ecosystem strategy stands today and where a Staff PM could move it fastest.

Jordan Alvarez
